name: How do you know if your property is a good candidate for an in-law suite?

mainEntity.name: How do you know if your property is a good candidate for an in-law suite?
mainEntity.text: How do you know if your property is a good candidate for an in-law suite?

acceptedAnswer.text: The best way to determine feasibility is to evaluate the lot, the existing structure, and the utility layout together. A good candidate usually has enough room for setbacks, access, drainage, and a functional entry path. Existing garages, basements, or underused rooms can make the project easier. The house should also have a structure that can support the desired changes without major reconstruction. Even a smaller lot may work if the design is efficient and the city allows the intended configuration. A professional feasibility review can quickly show whether the best path is a conversion, attached addition, or detached suite. That step helps homeowners avoid wasting money on a concept that will never fit the site well.
acceptedAnswer.description: A good candidate usually has workable setbacks, enough utility access, a structure that can be converted or expanded, and a layout that supports privacy and circulation. Flat or gently sloped lots are often easier, but older homes can still work if the underlying conditions are solid. A site review is the fastest way to confirm feasibility.
